newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - June 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - June 25.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Commission on Elections (Comelec) faces being declared in contempt by the Supreme Court if it gives a hearing to the petition of the People's Initiative for Reforms, Modernisation and Action to amend the Constitution and lift term limits set on the President and other elective officials, Representative Joker Arroyo said yesterday. The Comelec is scheduled to hear today the petition filed by the pro-charter change group. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)

- At least 13 more people were killed in Mindanao yesterday, bringing to 33 the number of fatalities in the military's renewed offensive against Moslem rebels even as the Moro Islamic Liberation Front threatened to walk out of its peace talks with the government. (STAR)
- Filipino troopers stationed on Kota Island, one of the disputed islands in the Spratly chain in the South China Sea, fired warning shots at a Chinese fishing vessel last Friday. (STANDARD)
- The Iranian government is set to invest in an oil refinery in Mindanao, said Nur Misuari, governor of the Autonomous Region for Moslem Mindanao. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)
- Local manufacturers yesterday warned the government of a continuous widening of the country's trade deficit due to increased importation of consumer goods by duty-free shops. (CHRONICLE/BULLETIN)

- The Securities and Exchange Commission is strengthening the agency's prosecution and enforcement department by giving it full powers to investigate companies violating SEC rules and regulations. (JOURNAL)
